section_summary: This section covers Japanese finances in 1940, chiefly a detailed report on the 1940–41 national budget, bond issues, military expenditure and colonial accounts. Other documents concern a proposed American-financed loan for Japanese ship purchases, a reported bond scheme using an American corporation, contributions to Japanese war funds in Seattle, and information about Italian funds intended for Hideo Ito.

subfiles.title: Instructions concerning proposed loan for Japanese ship purchases
subfiles.to: American Consulate General, Shanghai; repeated to Peiping and Chungking
subfiles.about: The Department requests more facts about a proposed $2 million loan for Japanese ship purchases.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks for the source and nature of the financing and suggests showing the interested Americans a Commerce Department statement on credit to Japanese firms.

subfiles.title: Recommendation on Shanghai financial transaction
subfiles.about: The division recommends no further action on the proposed Shanghai transaction.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai is informing the parties about U.S. guidance on credit to Japanese firms.

subfiles.title: Shanghai report on proposed ship-financing transaction
subfiles.about: William Hunt explains his companies’ role and possible funding sources for the proposed transaction.
subfiles.summary: Hunt says his companies hold no title to the vessels and that the Japanese parties have yet to act. He suggests consulting National City Bank in New York about any American funds involved.

subfiles.title: Reduction in Budget Expenditures for 1940–41
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Japan’s cabinet approved budget reductions totaling ¥642,187,000.
subfiles.summary: The despatch distinguishes canceled from postponed spending and lists affected accounts. It reports generally favorable press reaction, criticism that the cuts were superficial, and a fall in Tokyo share prices.

subfiles.title: Termination of proposed ship-financing agreement
subfiles.about: The China Foreign Trade Corporation declined to extend the agreement after it expired unused.
subfiles.summary: The corporation also considered the proposed transaction incompatible with existing conditions.

subfiles.title: National Budget for Japan—1940–41 Fiscal Year
subfiles.doc_type: commercial attaché report with translated budget tables
subfiles.from: Frank S. Williams, Commercial Attaché, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The report compiles Japan’s 1940–41 national budget, supplementary appropriations and special accounts.
subfiles.summary: It compares the general and extraordinary military budgets with prior years and estimates financing through bond issues. A translation of the promulgated budget details revenue and expenditure by ministry, followed by supplementary budgets and accounts for railways, debt, insurance and other activities. Separate tables cover Kwantung, Chosen, Taiwan, Karafuto and the South Seas Mandate, ending with the ¥4.46 billion contingent military expenditure budget.

subfiles.title: Reported premium-bond scheme using an American corporation
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: A Japanese group reportedly planned to issue lottery-like premium bonds in China through an American corporation.
subfiles.summary: The embassy identifies the International Finance and Exchange Company’s Delaware registration and original incorporators, and reports that Japanese participants intended to issue debentures under their names.

subfiles.title: Request for investigation of International Finance and Exchange Company
subfiles.to: American Consul, Tientsin; information to Peiping and Shanghai
subfiles.about: The Department requests an investigation of the corporation’s ownership, directors and proposed activities.
subfiles.summary: It identifies two American directors in Tientsin and asks for a report, with a copy to the U.S. district attorney at Shanghai if the bond plan proceeds.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of ship-purchase underwriting agreement
subfiles.from: Richard P. Butrick, American Consulate General, Shanghai
subfiles.about: Butrick forwards a confidential copy of the proposed ship-purchase financing agreement.
subfiles.summary: The agreement was supplied by the China Foreign Trade Corporation.

subfiles.title: Underwriting Agreement
subfiles.from: Taromatsu Kanda and Yutaro Sato, through Yoshimitsu Tatsuno; China Foreign Trade Corporation
subfiles.about: The corporation agrees to lend or underwrite up to $2 million for the purchasers’ acquisition of vessels.
subfiles.summary: The agreement sets a $1 million minimum, twelve-month repayment, eight-percent interest and security through a National City Bank letter of credit. It provides for termination if the purchasers do not act within a month and states that the transaction is commercial.

subfiles.title: Japanese Association of Seattle
subfiles.from: B. Phillips, Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.about: Naval Intelligence forwards a report on contributions collected by the Japanese Association of Seattle.
subfiles.summary: A copy of the report was also furnished to the Treasury Department.

subfiles.title: Japanese Association of Seattle: Contributions to Japanese War Funds
subfiles.about: The report records a Seattle fundraising campaign for Japan’s war with China.
subfiles.summary: It reports that collected funds were delivered to the Seattle Japanese Consulate on September 12.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Italian funds
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Hoover forwards information about Italian funds for Berle’s consideration.
subfiles.summary: The letter encloses a memorandum from a source Hoover considers reliable.

subfiles.title: Italian credit intended for Hideo Ito
subfiles.about: An Italian credit of $795,767.80 was reportedly to be withdrawn and secretly delivered to Hideo Ito.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum names a possible banking channel and Ito’s New York address.
